NASB.1: 'Call now, is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?
NASB.2: 'For anger slays the foolish man, And jealousy kills the simple.
NASB.3: 'I have seen the foolish taking root, And I cursed his abode immediately.
NASB.4: 'His sons are far from safety, They are even oppressed in the gate, And there is no deliverer.
NASB.5: 'His harvest the hungry devour And take it to a [place of] thorns, And the schemer is eager for their wealth.
NASB.6: 'For affliction does not come from the dust, Nor does trouble sprout from the ground,
NASB.7: For man is born for trouble, As sparks fly upward.
NASB.8: 'But as for me, I would seek God, And I would place my cause before God;
NASB.9: Who does great and unsearchable things, Wonders without number.
NASB.10: 'He gives rain on the earth And sends water on the fields,
NASB.11: So that He sets on high those who are lowly, And those who mourn are lifted to safety.
NASB.12: 'He frustrates the plotting of the shrewd, So that their hands cannot attain success.
NASB.13: 'He captures the wise by their own shrewdness, And the advice of the cunning is quickly thwarted.
NASB.14: 'By day they meet with darkness, And grope at noon as in the night.
NASB.15: 'But He saves from the sword of their mouth, And the poor from the hand of the mighty.
NASB.16: 'So the helpless has hope, And unrighteousness must shut its mouth.
NASB.17: 'Behold, how happy is the man whom God reproves, So do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
NASB.18: 'For He inflicts pain, and gives relief; He wounds, and His hands [also] heal.
NASB.19: 'From six troubles He will deliver you, Even in seven evil will not touch you.
NASB.20: 'In famine He will redeem you from death, And in war from the power of the sword.
NASB.21: 'You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, And you will not be afraid of violence when it comes.
NASB.22: 'You will laugh at violence and famine, And you will not be afraid of wild beasts.
NASB.23: 'For you will be in league with the stones of the field, And the beasts of the field will be at peace with you.
NASB.24: 'You will know that your tent is secure, For you will visit your abode and fear no loss.
NASB.25: 'You will know also that your descendants will be many, And your offspring as the grass of the earth.
NASB.26: 'You will come to the grave in full vigor, Like the stacking of grain in its season.
NASB.27: 'Behold this; we have investigated it, [and] so it is. Hear it, and know for yourself.'

NKJV.1: “Call out now; Is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?
NKJV.2: For wrath kills a foolish man, And envy slays a simple one.
NKJV.3: I have seen the foolish taking root, But suddenly I cursed his dwelling place.
NKJV.4: His sons are far from safety, They are crushed in the gate, And there is no deliverer.
NKJV.5: Because the hungry eat up his harvest, Taking it even from the thorns, And a snare snatches their substance.
NKJV.6: For affliction does not come from the dust, Nor does trouble spring from the ground;
NKJV.7: Yet man is born to trouble, As the sparks fly upward.
NKJV.8: “But as for me, I would seek God, And to God I would commit my cause—
NKJV.9: Who does great things, and unsearchable, Marvelous things without number.
NKJV.10: He gives rain on the earth, And sends waters on the fields.
NKJV.11: He sets on high those who are lowly, And those who mourn are lifted to safety.
NKJV.12: He frustrates the devices of the crafty, So that their hands cannot carry out their plans.
NKJV.13: He catches the wise in their own craftiness, And the counsel of the cunning comes quickly upon them.
NKJV.14: They meet with darkness in the daytime, And grope at noontime as in the night.
NKJV.15: But He saves the needy from the sword, From the mouth of the mighty, And from their hand.
NKJV.16: So the poor have hope, And injustice shuts her mouth.
NKJV.17: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects; Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
NKJV.18: For He bruises, but He binds up; He wounds, but His hands make whole.
NKJV.19: He shall deliver you in six troubles, Yes, in seven no evil shall touch you.
NKJV.20: In famine He shall redeem you from death, And in war from the power of the sword.
NKJV.21: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, And you shall not be afraid of destruction when it comes.
NKJV.22: You shall laugh at destruction and famine, And you shall not be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
NKJV.23: For you shall have a covenant with the stones of the field, And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.
NKJV.24: You shall know that your tent is in peace; You shall visit your dwelling and find nothing amiss.
NKJV.25: You shall also know that your descendants shall be many, And your offspring like the grass of the earth.
NKJV.26: You shall come to the grave at a full age, As a sheaf of grain ripens in its season.
NKJV.27: Behold, this we have searched out; It is true. Hear it, and know for yourself.”

ESV.1: “Call now; is there anyone who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
ESV.2: Surely vexation kills the fool, and jealousy slays the simple.
ESV.3: I have seen the fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling.
ESV.4: His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the gate, and there is no one to deliver them.
ESV.5: The hungry eat his harvest, and he takes it even out of thorns,  and the thirsty pant  after his  wealth.
ESV.6: For affliction does not come from the dust, nor does trouble sprout from the ground,
ESV.7: but man is born to trouble as the sparks fly upward.
ESV.8: “As for me, I would seek God, and to God would I commit my cause,
ESV.9: who does great things and unsearchable, marvelous things without number:
ESV.10: he gives rain on the earth and sends waters on the fields;
ESV.11: he sets on high those who are lowly, and those who mourn are lifted to safety.
ESV.12: He frustrates the devices of the crafty, so that their hands achieve no success.
ESV.13: He catches the wise in their own craftiness, and the schemes of the wily are brought to a quick end.
ESV.14: They meet with darkness in the daytime and grope at noonday as in the night.
ESV.15: But he saves the needy from the sword of their mouth and from the hand of the mighty.
ESV.16: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.
ESV.17: “Behold, blessed is the one whom God reproves; therefore despise not the discipline of the Almighty.
ESV.18: For he wounds, but he binds up; he shatters, but his hands heal.
ESV.19: He will deliver you from six troubles; in seven no evil  shall touch you.
ESV.20: In famine he will redeem you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
ESV.21: You shall be hidden from the lash of the tongue, and shall not fear destruction when it comes.
ESV.22: At destruction and famine you shall laugh, and shall not fear the beasts of the earth.
ESV.23: For you shall be in league with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.
ESV.24: You shall know that your tent is at peace, and you shall inspect your fold and miss nothing.
ESV.25: You shall know also that your offspring shall be many, and your descendants as the grass of the earth.
ESV.26: You shall come to your grave in ripe old age, like a sheaf gathered up in its season.
ESV.27: Behold, this we have searched out; it is true. Hear, and know it for your good.”

NLT.1:
“Cry for help, but will anyone answer you?
Which of the angels will help you?
NLT.2:
Surely resentment destroys the fool,
and jealousy kills the simple.
NLT.3:
I have seen that fools may be successful for the moment,
but then comes sudden disaster.
NLT.4:
Their children are abandoned far from help;
they are crushed in court with no one to defend them.
NLT.5:
The hungry devour their harvest,
even when it is guarded by brambles.
The thirsty pant after their wealth.
NLT.6:
But evil does not spring from the soil,
and trouble does not sprout from the earth.
NLT.7:
People are born for trouble
as readily as sparks fly up from a fire.
NLT.8:
“If I were you, I would go to God
and present my case to him.
NLT.9:
He does great things too marvelous to understand.
He performs countless miracles.
NLT.10:
He gives rain for the earth
and water for the fields.
NLT.11:
He gives prosperity to the poor
and protects those who suffer.
NLT.12:
He frustrates the plans of schemers
so the work of their hands will not succeed.
NLT.13:
He traps the wise in their own cleverness
so their cunning schemes are thwarted.
NLT.14:
They find it is dark in the daytime,
and they grope at noon as if it were night.
NLT.15:
He rescues the poor from the cutting words of the strong,
and rescues them from the clutches of the powerful.
NLT.16:
And so at last the poor have hope,
and the snapping jaws of the wicked are shut.
NLT.17:
“But consider the joy of those corrected by God!
Do not despise the discipline of the Almighty when you sin.
NLT.18:
For though he wounds, he also bandages.
He strikes, but his hands also heal.
NLT.19:
From six disasters he will rescue you;
even in the seventh, he will keep you from evil.
NLT.20:
He will save you from death in time of famine,
from the power of the sword in time of war.
NLT.21:
You will be safe from slander
and have no fear when destruction comes.
NLT.22:
You will laugh at destruction and famine;
wild animals will not terrify you.
NLT.23:
You will be at peace with the stones of the field,
and its wild animals will be at peace with you.
NLT.24:
You will know that your home is safe.
When you survey your possessions, nothing will be missing.
NLT.25:
You will have many children;
your descendants will be as plentiful as grass!
NLT.26:
You will go to the grave at a ripe old age,
like a sheaf of grain harvested at the proper time!
NLT.27:
“We have studied life and found all this to be true.
Listen to my counsel, and apply it to yourself.”

AMP.1:
"Call now—is there anyone who will answer you?
And to which of the holy ones (angels) will you turn?
AMP.2:
"For anger slays the foolish man,
And jealousy kills the simple (naive).
AMP.3:
"I have seen the foolish taking root [and outwardly prospering],
But I cursed his dwelling immediately [for his destruction was certain].
AMP.4:
"His children are far from safety [and included in their father's ruin],
They are oppressed and crushed in the [court of justice in the city's] gate,
And there is no one to rescue them.
AMP.5:
"The hungry devour his harvest
And take it even [when it grows] among the thorns;
The trap opens for [his] wealth.
AMP.6:
"For affliction does not come forth from the dust,
Nor does trouble spring forth from the ground.
AMP.7:
"For man is born for trouble,
[As naturally] as sparks fly upward.
AMP.8:
"As for me, I would seek God and inquire of Him,
And I would commit my cause to God;
AMP.9:
Who does great and unsearchable things,
Marvelous things without number.
AMP.10:
"He gives rain upon the earth
And sends waters upon the fields,
AMP.11:
So that He sets on high those who are lowly,
And He lifts to safety those who mourn.
AMP.12:
"He frustrates the devices and schemes of the crafty,
So that their hands cannot attain success or achieve anything of [lasting] worth.
AMP.13:
"He catches the [so-called] wise in their own shrewdness,
And the advice of the devious is quickly thwarted.
AMP.14:
"In the daytime they meet in darkness,
And at noon they grope as in the night.
AMP.15:
"But God saves [the innocent] from the sword of the mouth of the devious,
And the poor from the hand of the mighty.
AMP.16:
"So the helpless have hope,
And injustice shuts its mouth.
AMP.17:
"Behold, how happy and fortunate is the man whom God reproves,
So do not despise or reject the discipline of the Almighty [subjecting you to trial and suffering].
AMP.18:
"For He inflicts pain, but He binds up and gives relief;
He wounds, but His hands also heal.
AMP.19:
"He will rescue you from six troubles;
Even in seven, evil will not touch you.
AMP.20:
"In famine He will redeem you from death,
And in war from the power of the sword.
AMP.21:
"You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue,
And you will not be afraid of destruction when it comes.
AMP.22:
"You will laugh at violence and famine,
And you will not be afraid of the wild beasts of the earth.
AMP.23:
"For you will be in harmony with the stones of the field,
And the beasts of the field will be at peace with you.
AMP.24:
"You will know also that your tent is secure and at peace,
And you will visit your dwelling and fear no loss [nor find anything amiss].
AMP.25:
"You will know also that your descendants will be many,
And your offspring as the grass of the earth.
AMP.26:
"You will come to your grave in old age,
Like the stacking of grain [on the threshing floor] in its season.
AMP.27:
"Behold this; we have investigated it, and it is true.
Hear and heed it, and know for yourself [for your own good]."

MSG.1:
"Call for help, Job, if you think anyone will answer!
To which of the holy angels will you turn?
MSG.2:
The hot temper of a fool eventually kills him,
the jealous anger of a simpleton does her in.
MSG.3:
I've seen it myself—seen fools putting down roots,
and then, suddenly, their houses are cursed.
MSG.4:
Their children out in the cold, abused and exploited,
with no one to stick up for them.
MSG.5:
Hungry people off the street plunder their harvests,
cleaning them out completely, taking thorns and all,
insatiable for everything they have.
MSG.6:
Don't blame fate when things go wrong—
trouble doesn't come from nowhere.
MSG.7:
It's human! Mortals are born and bred for trouble,
as certainly as sparks fly upward.
MSG.8:
"If I were in your shoes, I'd go straight to God,
I'd throw myself on the mercy of God.
MSG.9:
After all, he's famous for great and unexpected acts;
there's no end to his surprises.
MSG.10:
He gives rain, for instance, across the wide earth,
sends water to irrigate the fields.
MSG.11:
He raises up the down-and-out,
gives firm footing to those sinking in grief.
MSG.12:
He aborts the schemes of conniving crooks,
so that none of their plots come to term.
MSG.13:
He catches the know-it-alls in their conspiracies—
all that intricate intrigue swept out with the trash!
MSG.14:
Suddenly they're disoriented, plunged into darkness;
they can't see to put one foot in front of the other.
MSG.15:
But the downtrodden are saved by God,
saved from the murderous plots, saved from the iron fist.
MSG.16:
And so the poor continue to hope,
while injustice is bound and gagged.
MSG.17:
"So, what a blessing when God steps in and corrects you!
Mind you, don't despise the discipline of Almighty God!
MSG.18:
True, he wounds, but he also dresses the wound;
the same hand that hurts you, heals you.
MSG.19:
From one disaster after another he delivers you;
no matter what the calamity, the evil can't touch you—
MSG.20:
"In famine, he'll keep you from starving,
in war, from being gutted by the sword.
MSG.21:
You'll be protected from vicious gossip
and live fearless through any catastrophe.
MSG.22:
You'll shrug off disaster and famine,
and stroll fearlessly among wild animals.
MSG.23:
You'll be on good terms with rocks and mountains;
wild animals will become your good friends.
MSG.24:
You'll know that your place on earth is safe,
you'll look over your goods and find nothing amiss.
MSG.25:
You'll see your children grow up,
your family lovely and lissome as orchard grass.
MSG.26:
You'll arrive at your grave ripe with many good years,
like sheaves of golden grain at harvest.
MSG.27:
"Yes, this is the way things are—my word of honor!
Take it to heart and you won't go wrong."

NET.1: “Call now! Is there anyone who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

NET.3: I myself have seen the fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his place of residence.
NET.4: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed at the place where judgment is rendered, nor is there anyone to deliver them.

NET.7: but people are born to trouble, as surely as the sparks fly upward.

NET.9: He does great and unsearchable things, marvelous things without number;
NET.10: he gives rain on the earth, and sends water on the fields;
NET.11: he sets the lowly on high, that those who mourn are raised to safety.
NET.12: He frustrates the plans of the crafty so that their hands cannot accomplish what they had planned!
NET.13: He catches the wise in their own craftiness, and the counsel of the cunning is brought to a quick end.
